# stackit_observability_cert_check (Resource)

Observability certificate check resource schema. Certificate checks are unique per source within an instance: creating a check for a source that already exists returns the existing check. Two resources with the same `source` therefore manage the same check, and destroying one of them deletes it. Not every Observability plan allows certificate checks (e.g. `Observability-Monitoring-Starter-EU01` does not). Must have a `region` specified in the provider configuration. This service is only available when the provider is configured with `default_region = "eu01"`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stackit_observability_cert_check" "example" {
  project_id  = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
  instance_id = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
  source      = "tcp://www.example.com:443"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The Observability instance ID to which the certificate check is associated.
- `project_id` (String) STACKIT project ID to which the certificate check is associated.
- `source` (String) The endpoint whose certificate is checked, including the port, e.g. `tcp://www.example.com:443` or `https://www.example.com:443`.

### Read-Only

- `cert_check_id` (String) The certificate check ID.
- `id` (String) Terraform's internal resource ID. It is structured as "`project_id`,`instance_id`,`cert_check_id`".

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [` + "`" + `import` + "`" + ` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the ` + "`" + `id` + "`" + ` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Only use the import statement, if you want to import an existing observability cert check
import {
  to = stackit_observability_cert_check.import-example
  id = "${var.project_id},${var.observability_instance_id},${var.observability_cert_check_id}"
}
```
